A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same survey, with matching authors, title and core organization. All pages, figures and tables support comparison. Neither PDF contains an appendix.

before.justification: v1 presents a literature survey and conceptual taxonomy. Its empirical findings are attributed to cited studies; it reports no original experiments or empirical data analysis.

after.justification: v2 remains a survey. Its new classification matrix and synthesis are conceptual literature analysis, while reported performance outcomes remain attributed to cited studies.

M1.justification: Neither version proposes a concrete routing algorithm of its own. The new three-stage pipeline in Section 10 synthesizes existing approaches; additional descriptions of cited methods do not establish a changed proposed method.

E1.justification: LLMRouterBench and additional translation and multimodal studies expand the literature reviewed. Neither version actually conducts training or evaluation on these datasets or tasks.

E2.justification: Neither version evaluates a proposed method against a comparator set. Newly mentioned comparisons, including GreenServ versus random routing, belong to cited studies.

E3.justification: Neither survey introduces or revises an experimental protocol. The evaluation-metric overview in Section 9.2 is retained; settings described for newly cited studies are not experiments conducted by this work.

E4.justification: No ablations, robustness tests, sensitivity experiments or empirical case studies are added or removed. Section 10 supplies conceptual examples and interpretation rather than supplementary experimental analysis.

E5.justification: No repeated-run counts, seeds, confidence intervals, significance tests or statistical reporting practices are added or revised. Discussion of model confidence concerns routing methods, not uncertainty estimates for experimental results.

E6.justification: v2 removes GraphRouter's 'minimum 12.3% gain' and UniRoute's 'more than 30' unseen-model count. It adds cited GreenServ results of 22% higher accuracy and 31% lower energy consumption versus random routing, with under 8 ms routing overhead, and reports ReLope and Attention Probe outperforming existing probes across five benchmarks. These are changes to reported literature findings, not new same-setting evaluations by the survey authors.

T1.justification: No formal definitions, assumptions, theorems, proofs or derivations are introduced or revised. The added design-space synthesis and descriptions of theoretical ideas remain conceptual explanations.

C1.justification: The abstract is unchanged. The introduction and conclusion retain the multi-LLM scope, six-paradigm taxonomy, three-axis conceptual framework and claims about exploiting model complementarity.

C2.justification: New Section 10 develops a substantial interpretation through pre-routing, verification and escalation stages, then advances research-gap claims concerning response-aware online adaptation, learned cascade policies and joint multi-objective optimization. Section 1.4 also clarifies overlapping routing stages and distinguishes deployment-time bandits from training-time policy optimization.

D1.justification: The expanded summary table adds mechanism and training-data information, including Cascade Routing's log-probability-based query-response data. v2 also removes v1's direct Arch-Router model-access footnote from Section 3. These are documentation and access-information changes.

R1.justification: v2 substantially expands coverage through RouteLMT, ICL-Router, IRT-Router, SCOPE, GreenServ, ReLope and LLMRouterBench, alongside additional translation research. This broadens discussion of model representations, energy-aware routing and multimodal deployment. Dekoninck's 2024-to-2025 citation update refers to the same previously cited work.

P1.justification: Most existing prose and section ordering remain intact. v2 adds explanatory passages and a synthesis section before the conclusion, with localized terminology, wording and cross-reference revisions.

P2.justification: v2 adds a substantial color-coded design-space matrix as Table 1, comparing methods across timing, input signals and decision mechanisms. The previous summary table becomes Table 2 and expands from 25 to 30 methods. Figures 1–3 retain their artwork and captions while relocating with text reflow.

improvement.justification: The new matrix and Section 10 make v1's conceptual framework more explicit and useful for comparing routing designs. GreenServ and ReLope also fill concrete coverage gaps concerning energy-aware and multimodal routing. These gains outweigh the small loss of access convenience from removing the Arch-Router model link, supporting a limited overall improvement.
